claims.text: Wrap the awaited appStore import in error handling - dynamic imports can reject and without try/catch this will throw and interrupt the refund flow (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:967)

In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts lines 589-596, app resolution and PaymentService instantiation happen outside the try-catch block - if either fails, the error bypasses handleRefundError leaving refund flow incomplete
The hand-maintained list of 28 apps in packages/app-store/index.ts has no gating test to keep it in sync with the generated app list.
Wrap the awaited appStore import in error handling so a failed async import doesn't throw past this function without context (packages/lib/payment/handlePayment.ts:26)
On cal.com's actual deployment runtime (Next.js server / Vercel serverless), will an unhandled rejected promise be swallowed, logged, or will it terminate the process?
apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) pushes the resolved value (not a promise), so it won't actually be awaited downstream in the Promise.all
Wrap the awaited appStore lookup in error handling so a failed dynamic import doesn't throw out of deletePayment without a controlled response (packages/lib/payment/deletePayment.ts:16)

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
The calendar property in packages/core/CalendarManager.ts now holds Promise<Calendar | null> but property name doesn't indicate async nature - may confuse consumers expecting resolved Calendar object
wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts uses forEach(async ...) which doesn't await calendar deletions - same issue as vital/lib/reschedule.ts where forEach discards returned Promises
The for loop in getVideoAdapters serializes adapter loads, reducing performance compared to parallel loading
Wrap the awaited appStore lookup with error handling so a failed async import doesn't throw out of the cancellation flow (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:589)

All dynamic imports are evaluated immediately when the module is first required, so all 28 app bundles begin loading in parallel at startup - no true lazy loading benefit is achieved. Should use thunk functions (() => import(...)) so modules are only fetched when first accessed.
Handle errors from the awaited getCalendar call - rejected import will bubble out of createEvent without any recovery or logging (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:233)
Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

Dynamic imports in packages/app-store/index.ts are still eager - each import() runs when module is evaluated, so importing appStore kicks off every provider load immediately instead of true on-demand loading

getCalendarCredentials remains a synchronous function, but the `calendar` field on its returned object is now a Promise instead of `Calendar | null`, which is misleading given the field name and the unchanged type alias consumers rely on.
A commented-out example entry was translated into the new import syntax but still points to a directory that doesn't exist.
getVideoAdapters awaits inside a loop; once F-001's fix (switching to thunks) lands, this loop will become genuinely sequential module loading instead of a no-op await.
Handle errors from the awaited appStore import so a failed dynamic import doesn't surface as an unhandled rejection (packages/app-store/_utils/getCalendar.ts:15)
What is the actual measured impact of this change on cold start time and server bundle size?
Handle failures from getCalendar - awaited call is not wrapped in error handling so rejected import inside async callback will go uncaught (packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:128)

vital/lib/reschedule.ts uses forEach(async ...) which doesn't await calendar deletions - forEach ignores the Promise returned by async callbacks, so deleteEvent calls run as detached fire-and-forget tasks and errors become unhandled Promise rejections
In handleCancelBooking.ts:458, apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) pushes the resolved value rather than a Promise, so Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) will not wait for the deletions

The awaited getCalendar call has no error handling inside the async callback - if it rejects the error becomes unhandled because callback promise isn't awaited (packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts:128)
